NOT INDEPENDENTLY RESTORED — reviewed, and correctly so: this isn't persistent state to restore, it's set fresh at every real checksum from action?.Id (NetFullCombatState.cs:396), where `action` is whichever GameAction ChecksumTracker.GenerateChecksum just finished (ChecksumTracker.cs:160, ObtainAndTrackChecksum calls NetFullCombatState.FromRun(_runState, action); GenerateChecksum(NetFullCombatState) at ChecksumTracker.cs:295-301 hashes the full serialized bytes with XxHash32, so this field genuinely is part of the real cross-peer checksum, not just diagnostics). Its post-restore correctness instead depends entirely on ActionQueueSet's action-id counter, which ChecksumHook.SyncPoint.NextActionId already tracks — and RestoreTo deliberately does NOT rewind it. See RestoreTo's own extensive comment on NextActionId: rewinding it was MEASURED, on a live 2-instance run, to cause exactly this kind of post-restore mismatch (host nextActionId=9 vs client nextActionId=12 at the same checksum id, diverging at the very next checksum), and leaving it unrewound — letting each peer's counter keep climbing independently — was the fix, with the tradeoff explicitly acknowledged: 'the next action after it is checksummed and compared as usual, just under a fresh id, so an asymmetric restore still shows up immediately.' This is the already-reviewed, already-measured design (see also the ChecksumHook.cs SyncPoint.RewardIds field doc comment for the parallel ChoiceIds treatment, and the UndoSync commit history: "multiplayer undo harness, two real fixes, and one open divergence" -> "multiplayer undo verified clean"), not an unreviewed gap in this ledger's scope.

NOT INDEPENDENTLY RESTORED — same shape as lastExecutedActionId above: set fresh per-real-checksum from (action as GenericHookGameAction)?.HookId (NetFullCombatState.cs:395), not persistent state. Its post-restore correctness depends on ActionQueueSynchronizer's hook-id counter, which SyncPoint.NextHookId DOES capture and RestoreTo DOES restore, via ActionQueueSynchronizer.FastForwardHookId(sp.NextHookId) — flagged in RestoreTo's own comment as 'a reading of the code, not a measurement': unlike NextActionId, no live 2-instance run has yet exercised a hook action across a restore to confirm this counter is actually peer-common. Tracked via NextHookId, not independently captured here; the still-open verification is on NextHookId's own comment in ChecksumHook.cs, not a new gap.
